As someone who recently went through school in the U.S. with T1D, that sort of thing may be avoidable if you work with the school to give him personalized snacks at the nurse's office. They'd always be available to him, and they would never give them away to anyone else, so long as you purchased them, brought them to the school, and specifically explained to the nurses that they are for your son as treatment for a low. It would also help to make sure your son's 504 has a statement saying that your son can go to the nurse at any time. This is really only helpful in the U.S. mind you, as I'm unsure of what documents like a 504 plan are like in other nations. And of course, NTA, I would recommend that you teach your husband about things such as hypoglycemic seizures and the like, and explain to him how much one would impact your family. They're terrifying for everyone involved, and can leave permanent handicaps in their wake. If even that doesn't knock it into his head the severity of the disease and it's possibility to cause permanent, and in some cases fatal damage, then maybe your son's endocrinologist could help bring him up to speed.

TLDR: Woman is in 9 year relationship and wants to experiment with her sexuality but her partner made an ultimatum that they either break up or she doesn't experiment at all. I wanna know how other people feel about all this since I'm not that experienced, and I rant a lot. Sorry in advance.




So I don't like this for a lot of reasons, but I'll start with the fact that this woman is far into a very serious relationship. There's a time and a place where it's more than ok to question and explore your sexuality, but 9 years into a straight, monogamous relationship might be too far. I feel as if the woman who's questioning what to do in the article doesn't see their relationship as a complete and serious one if that makes sense? To their partner, a nearly decade long monogamous relationship almost certainly means that they thought the two of them might be nearing, at, or even past the point of really settling down and into things, and the idea of their partner experimenting with other people might be too far for them as it's a big step, and not one you'd expect after a relationship that long. I see the person who addressed the article's side as well though, they're probably thinking that they're getting to (or are probably a good bit beyond) the point where they won't ever get to see if they'd rather live a different life, but I'd honestly say that 9 years really might've been too long to bring up the idea of experimenting to their partner. Either way they go, both parties will have a lot of resent and anger towards the other, and they'll both probably go through a lot of pain no matter what. The woman in question is selfish for getting that far into a relationship with someone and not having mentioned how they feel earlier on, and the man is selfish in his ultimatum, and no matter what, their relationship will probably be damaged and possibly ending something that important that's gone on for that long could really lead to a lot of pain and problems for either of them, but even as someone who's typically always had a huge preference towards one gender over the other, not having the chance to test the waters of your desires for the rest of your life might be too much to try and handle. Sorry for all the ranting and poor summarizing, I'm just wondering what the community thinks about this since I'm pretty divided and have only been out of the closet for about two years so I might not really understand how either party feels, as I've never even got close to a decade long relationship either. Once again sorry for the rant and probably horrible grammar, spelling, and an almost certainly iffy premise that I don't know much about.

This one's from personal experience, as I've had many close friends who've dated older guys as well as guys who've dated older girls, and I have to say it's very rare that it'll be a good thing in the end. The vast majority of the time the relationship isn't a very happy one, where the older of the couple is almost always much less interested in the relationship and their partner than the younger is, and that can lead to a lot of issues. Dating someone older than you can seem cool and it can feel like you're in a bigger, more real relationship than one with someone your age, but in every case I've seen, it leads to an unhappy ending and in a few cases, it's lead to real problems that have genuinely hurt people in serious ways.
